messages:
Alex: Heads-up — we've seen another wave of flaky cards in us-west-2 last night. Hard to triage quickly from app alerts alone. Thinking we need a standardized on-node collector that parses dmesg/journalctl + periodic nvidia-smi snapshots and emits compact event-lines to logging.
Maria: +1. Current scattershot approach (manual ssh + `dmesg | grep -i xid`) is too slow. Proposal: small agent that only emits GPU health events (Xid, ECC corrected/unc, NVML warnings) as JSONL to our logging pipeline. Keeps logs small and indexable.
Jin: I sketched a minimal pipeline in the spike:
```
- tail kernel ring buffer (dmesg -w --color=never)
- filter lines matching: /NVRM: Xid|error|GPU has a bad page|ECC error/
- poll `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,fan.speed,temperature.gpu,driver_model,retired_pages_info --format=csv,noheader` every 30s
- query NVML for corrected/uncorrected ECC counters every 60s
- emit single JSON line per event: {ts, node, gpu_index, type, code, raw_line} to fluent-bit input
```
Maria: Example journalctl / journal filter that works in prod: `journalctl -k -u kernel -o short-iso | grep -Ei "NVRM|Xid|ecc|GPU fault"` but we should avoid raw greps in prod. The agent needs built-in patterns: `Xid ([0-9]+): (.*)` and `GPU([0-9]+):.*retired page` to capture gpu index.
ops-bot: Alert posted: GPU ERROR RATE spike on node gpu-prod-45 (alert id #A-9923). Current Xid count 3 in 5m.
SRE_Jen: Proposed triage rules (automated):
- if a single GPU reports >= 5 Xid (any code) in a 10m sliding window -> tag node `gpu:flaky` and create ticket auto (low priority), annotate node in k8s (label + event)
- if a GPU reports >= 2 Xid of code 31 or shows uncorrectable ECC -> immediate cordon + drain and page oncall
- if multiple GPUs on the same host show retired_pages_info non-empty -> schedule replace and set host decommissioning flag
Alex: Can the agent also compute per-GPU error-rate / hour metrics so we can graph and alert more intelligently? Need a summary metric rather than raw flood.
Jin: Yes — agent maintains a small in-memory sliding window (exponential decay) and emits a metric every minute like `gpu.xid.count.1m` and `gpu.ecc.uncorrected.1m`. We can push to metrics backend with tags {node,gpu_index,region}.
Maria: Cost/retention note: emit only structured events + minor periodic snapshots. Avoid sending full dmesg all the time. Keep raw verbose logs at node for 7d, central JSONL events for 90d. Sampling policy: full `nvidia-smi -q` only on errors; otherwise emit lightweight `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv` every 30s.
Alex: Example event JSON (single-line):
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-02T03:12:14Z","node":"gpu-prod-45","gpu_index":"1","type":"XID","code":"31","msg":"NVRM: Xid (31) 00000000, PID 1234 ...","nvml":{ "ecc_uncorrected":0, "ecc_corrected":12 }}
```
SRE_Jen: Runbook additions: how to triage quickly from events:
- Step 1: open Kibana query `node:gpu-prod-45 AND gpu_index:1 and type:XID` (last 1h).
- Step 2: check `nvml.ecc_uncorrected > 0` -> cordon and page if true.
- Step 3: check retired_pages_info in last 24h -> mark host for replacement, do not reprovision onto same rack until hardware swap.
- Step 4: if only corrected ECC or isolated single Xid -> schedule job to repro/soak test the card (run `cuda_device_query` + 2h memtest).
Jin: Implementation notes:
- Prefer a tiny compiled agent (Rust/Go) that keeps footprint <20MB and uses journald API directly (no `grep`), plus NVML bindings.
- Output line protocol: newline-delimited JSON, include stable fields: ts,node,gpu_index,type,code,msg,ecc_corrected,ecc_uncorrected,sample_temp
- Fluent-bit tail input -> central logstore (index only event fields). For metrics route, push counters to Prometheus pushgateway on emergency, or emit into vector/otel for scraping.
Maria: Regex samples for dmesg parsing: `NVRM: Xid (\d+) 0x[0-9a-f]+, PID (\d+).*` and `GPU (\d+):.*retired page at.*` — need to test these across driver versions. Agent should include driver-version compatibility matrix.
Alex: Ops question — who owns the roll-out? I can do the initial agent PR + health dashboard if Jin and Maria sign off on parsing rules.
Jin: I'll own NVML sampling + metrics export. Maria can own parsing and indexing schema.
SRE_Jen: I'll add automated actions to the oncall playbook and add thresholds to alerting. Also add a synthetic that simulates Xid bursts so we can test runbook.
Maria: One more: ensure agent respects node-local log rotation and doesn't blow up disk. Keep circular buffer for raw logs and rotate every 24h.
Alex: Sweet. Next steps:
- Alex: open design RFC with parsing rules + sample events (this thread is the draft) -> 1763201234-rfc-gpu-health-agent (I'll create)
- Jin: spike NVML exporter and sampling PR by EOD Friday
- Maria: test regexes across 4 driver versions and post results in this thread next week
- SRE_Jen: add playbook hooks + synthetic test ticket
ops-bot: CI: gpu-health-agent-unit-tests passed (job #3421) :white_check_mark:
